recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Future changes to Group, HealthcareService, DeviceDefinition, or broader actor policy should be handled through the later workflow/security issues that govern those actor lists, not by reopening this R5 reconciliation.
issue_request: FHIR-32454 was Published as Persuasive with Modification for R5. It asked whether AuditEvent subjects should be represented as agents and whether AuditEvent/Provenance agent.who should include Group, CareTeam, and HealthCareService-like actors. The approved resolution clarified that subjects are recorded as entities unless they actively participate, and that .agent.who should recognize all Event pattern performer.actor types.
initial_application: Git commit 8209c17a869cab7d8ebb44b093fd235edf90c1c6 appears to be the initial application. It changed both source/auditevent/structuredefinition-AuditEvent.xml and source/provenance/structuredefinition-Provenance.xml, adding Event actor target profiles, including CareTeam, to agent.who.
additional_context: AuditEvent and Provenance are active current-build resources in source/fhir.ini. The current Event pattern performer.actor source lists Practitioner, PractitionerRole, Organization, CareTeam, Patient, Device, and RelatedPerson, and both current agent.who definitions include all of those. Later actor-policy work, including FHIR-49304/FHIR-49672 and commits 390878350715eca86888de3f0cfe40e5cec1200c and 7e693f8d597308c8f606d1725c0542c03b0d2240, added or confirmed additional agent types such as Group, HealthcareService, and DeviceDefinition where applicable. The separate subject/patient question raised during FHIR-32454 was split into FHIR-33155.
reconciliation: Published an empty audit commit and made no source changes because the authoritative StructureDefinition sources already satisfy the seed resolution.
